text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Bulgarian and Yugoslav parliamentarians meeting in Sofia will outline new direction in the expansion of bilateral cooperation.
- U.S. charge d'affaires in Belgrade visited Beogradska Banka AD to discuss normalisation of the bank's relations with U.S. financial institutions.
- German business delegation visited Yugoslavia's biggest port, Luka Bar, and expressed interest for offering consulting services in privatisation.
- Court hearing continues in Cyprus on Slovenia's request to freeze Yugoslavia's assets in the Cyprus Beogradska Banka until the end of succession talks between former Yugoslav republics.
- Some 200,000 people got jobs from January to mid-September, according to the Serbian labour market office.
- Speedy development and modernisation of the economy lie ahead of us, says Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic at the inauguration of several specialised fairs in Belgrade.
- The 21st century will be dominated by the left, said president of the directorate of the Yugoslav left (JUL) Mira Markovic.
NASA BORBA

- Former Yugoslav central bank governor Dragoslav Avramovic visited striking workers in the IMT motor and tractor industry saying that their demands require changes in the entire society and a new economic policy.
- Kragujevac Zastava arms workers continue strike because their promised outstanding holiday pay failed to materialise.
- Sugar could be Serbia's major export commodity, and the country plans to produce 710,000 tonnes a year of which 300,000 would be exported, the Serbian chamber of economy said.
- Hearing starts in the Paris commercial court over Slovenia's demand to freeze assets of the National bank of the former Yugoslavia in nine commercial banks in France.
- Board of directors of Serbian electricity industry decided to raise power prices by 50 percent from October 1.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Winter time starts on Sunday, September 29, when the clock will be moved back one hour, according to the decision of the federal government.
BORBA
- Metals giant Trepca of Kosovska Mitrovica and Greek firm Evangelos Mitilineos sign a $135 million worth deal for the export of Trepca products over a two-year period.
